label: trait causal graph
definition: A directed graph of evidence-backed causal or mechanistic relationships that explains how a microbial trait is realized; consists of typed nodes (traits, genes/proteins, chemicals, processes, environmental factors) connected by predicate-labeled edges.
traits_addressed: root domain class for the TraitMech causal-graph subsystem

label: trait causal node
definition: A typed entity that participates in a trait causal graph, addressable by a stable local identifier and bearing a category drawn from a controlled vocabulary of mechanism axes (trait, pathway, gene/protein, chemical, environmental factor, etc.).

label: trait causal edge
definition: An evidence-backed directed relationship between two trait causal nodes, carrying a predicate label (optionally grounded in an external relation ontology) and at least one citation supporting the causal claim.

label: trait causal node type
definition: The semantic category of a node in a trait causal graph; partitions causal-graph nodes by the kind of biological or chemical entity they denote.

label: causal-graph trait node
definition: A trait causal node that denotes a microbial trait (a METPO or TraitMech-registered trait); used in causal graphs to express how one trait depends on or modulates another.

label: causal-graph pathway node
definition: A trait causal node that denotes a metabolic or signaling pathway, or a pathway-like mechanism, that participates in the realization of a trait.

label: causal-graph environmental factor node
definition: A trait causal node that denotes an environmental exposure or condition (e.g. temperature, salinity, presence of a substrate) that contributes to or modulates the trait outcome.

label: causal-graph experimental factor node
definition: A trait causal node that denotes an assay, perturbation, treatment, or experimental condition under which the trait is observed or tested.

label: causal-graph gene or protein node
definition: A trait causal node that denotes a gene, protein, gene product, or protein complex implicated in the mechanism of a trait.

label: causal-graph chemical node
definition: A trait causal node that denotes a chemical entity (small molecule, ion, metabolite) participating in a trait mechanism — typically a substrate, product, cofactor, or electron donor/acceptor.

label: causal-graph organelle node
definition: A trait causal node that denotes a microbial subcellular organelle or organelle-like compartment relevant to the trait mechanism (e.g. magnetosome, carboxysome, gas vesicle).

label: causal-graph cellular localization node
definition: A trait causal node that denotes a cellular component or subcellular localization (cytoplasm, membrane, periplasm, cell wall, etc.) at which a trait mechanism is realized.

label: causal-graph molecular function node
definition: A trait causal node that denotes a molecular activity or function (catalysis, transport, binding) contributing to the trait mechanism.

label: causal-graph biological process node
definition: A trait causal node that denotes a biological process (e.g. respiration, nitrogen fixation, biofilm formation) that is part of, or causally upstream of, the trait mechanism.

label: causal-graph state node
definition: A trait causal node that denotes a bioenergetic or molecular state of the cell — a gradient or steady-value (e.g. proton motive force, redox state of the quinone pool) that mediates the trait mechanism. Distinct from a process: the state is the thing maintained, not its establishment.

label: causal-graph quality node
definition: A trait causal node that denotes a quality or measurable attribute of a cellular component (PATO-style axis attached to a microbial entity) — e.g. membrane fluidity, GC content, motility speed — that modulates the trait mechanism.

label: causal-graph capacity node
definition: A trait causal node that denotes a metabolic or functional capacity — an electron-donating pool, ATP charge, or other reservoir-of-X notion that is neither a single chemical species nor a process (e.g. reducing power, energy charge).
